title: Information Cascades in the Laboratory
description: Participants sequentially predict which urn generated private light or dark draws. Later participants observe earlier public predictions but not earlier private draws, allowing rational information cascades to form.

included: equal prior probability of urn A and urn B
random decision order in every period
implementation_scope.reason: The published appendix fully specifies the symmetric baseline. It does not provide the complete session-level schedule or raw data needed to reproduce every public-draw variant exactly.

findings.main_hypothesis: When prior public decisions create a sufficiently strong imbalance, later participants often follow the cascade even when their private signal points to the other urn.
Sequential public decisions improve information-use efficiency relative to decisions based only on private signals.
